lines.japanese: オーケイ、強引に行ってみよう。
lines.english: Okay. Time for the hard sell.

lines.japanese: 「はっ！　そうだ、そんなことより！」
lines.english: “Ah! Right—more importantly!”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　どうしたんだい、締め切り間近のライターがばったり編集さんに出くわしたような顔して」
lines.english: “Hm? What's wrong? You look like a writer on the eve of his deadline who's just run smack into his editor.”

lines.japanese: 「い、いえ、それが──」
lines.english: “W-well, you see—”

lines.japanese: 話を円滑に進めるため、残念ながら（俺狙いうちの）生々しい例えは無視させていただきます。
lines.english: For the sake of moving the conversation along, I shall regrettably ignore that painfully vivid—and personally targeted—analogy.

lines.japanese: 「──ふと、こんな噂を思いだしたんです。ある料理店にて、虐げられていた女給にまつわる話なんですが」
lines.english: “—I suddenly remembered a certain rumor. It concerns a waitress who was cruelly mistreated at a certain restaurant...”

lines.japanese: 「な、なにそれ。もしかして怖い話？　怖い話はしないでよ」
lines.english: “W-what kind of rumor? Is it a scary story? Don't tell a scary story.”

lines.japanese: 「うさんくせーなー。ソレつまんないオチだったら、休憩時間ムダにした分買いとってもらうかんなー？」
lines.english: “Sounds fishy. If this ends with some lame punch line, you owe me for every minute of my break you wasted. Got it?”

lines.japanese: 片や身を縮めて恐怖に震える女性、片や背もたれにどっかと体を預けてふんぞり返る女性。分かりやすいくらいキャラを守ってくれるお二人です。
lines.english: One woman curled up trembling in fear. The other leaned way back against the seat and sprawled out. They sure made their roles easy to read.

lines.japanese: 「その店には女性の給仕係が三人おりまして……その一人を仮におたまさんとしておきましょうか」
lines.english: “This restaurant employed three waitresses... and one of them, for the purposes of our tale, we shall call Tama.”

lines.japanese: 「おたまさんは、常日頃から謹直な姿勢を極端に重んじるあまり、同僚の給仕たちから疎んじられておりました。そしていつしか仲間の輪からも弾かれ、孤独の海に溺れる日々……」
lines.english: “Tama placed such extreme value on upright conduct in her daily life that her fellow waitresses came to shun her. Before long, she had been cast out of their circle altogether, left to drown day after day in a sea of solitude...”

lines.japanese: 「あー、いるよなそういうの。融通利かないっつーか、空気読めないっつーか。いるいる。そらアレだ、疎外とかじゃなく、単に自分から溶けこもうって心構えがなってないだけだ」
lines.english: “Oh, yeah, you get people like that. Inflexible, can't read the room—whatever. Sure, sure. That's not being ostracized. That's somebody who never learned how to make an effort to fit in.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなある日、おたまさんは休憩時間に混ぜてもらえない悔しさから、事務机にあったカッターを手に取っていきなり自分の首筋をズバーッ！」
lines.english: “Then one day, bitter at being barred from the others' break, Tama snatched up a box cutter from the office desk and—without warning—slashed it straight across her own throat!”

lines.japanese: 「キャーッ！」
lines.english: “Eeeek!”

lines.japanese: 「それ以来その店では、女ふたりで休憩をとっていると、後ろの壁からおたまさんに覗かれているかのような悪寒に襲われるというのです」
lines.english: “From that day forward, whenever two women took their break together at that restaurant, a terrible chill would seize them—as though Tama were peering through the wall behind their backs...”

lines.japanese: 「面白味がない上に覗き癖まであんのか、そいつ。救いようがねーな」
lines.english: “So she was boring and a peeping creep? There's no saving that woman.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うう……なんでいきなりそんな話を……？」
lines.english: “U-ugh... Why would you suddenly tell us something like that...?”

lines.japanese: 「何故って……だってほら……いまも紀奈子さんの後ろに……」
lines.english: “Why...? Well, because... even now, just behind you, Kinako...”

lines.japanese: <8>\「黒い影があああ！」
lines.english: “A BLACK SHADOOOOW!”

lines.japanese: 「キャーッ！」
lines.english: “Eeeek!”

lines.japanese: 「おまえの顔のが怖えーよ！」
lines.english: “Your face is scarier than the ghost!”

lines.japanese: 「なーんてことがないように我々も気を付けたいですね、っと」
lines.english: Let's all be careful not to let anything like that happen, okay?

lines.japanese: 恐怖を演出するために崩してしまった美貌を整えながら、俺はよっこらしょと椅子へ座りなおしました。
lines.english: Having restored the handsome features I had contorted to create the proper terror, I lowered myself back into my chair with a heave-ho.

lines.japanese: 「で？　はん、要はたまひよ仲間外れにすんなって言いたいの？」
lines.english: “So? Hah. You mean we shouldn't leave Tama-chick out, is that it?”

lines.japanese: さすが英里子さん。我ながらイマイチな怪談くずれの駄コントで、こちらの真意を汲み取ってくれました。
lines.english: As expected of Eriko. From the wreckage of my mediocre would-be ghost story and dreadful little skit, she had divined my true purpose.

lines.japanese: 「冗談。別にうちら、疎外してるわけじゃないから」
lines.english: “Kidding. We're not actually shutting her out or anything.”

lines.japanese: 「だよー、もー、失礼なー」
lines.english: “Exactly. Jeez, that's rude.”

lines.japanese: 正気を取り戻した紀奈子さんも、俺の訴えをさも不服と言わんばかりに、隣でうんうんと頷いていらっしゃいます。
lines.english: Kinako, now restored to her senses, nodded vigorously beside her, as though my accusation had offended her deeply.

lines.japanese: 「だってほら、三人もいっぺんに休憩入ったら、フロアの方が大変じゃない」
lines.english: “Besides, if all three of us went on break at once, the floor would be in trouble, wouldn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「ま、確かにそれはそうなんですけどね」
lines.english: Well, yeah, that's true.

lines.japanese: 納得せざるをえない理由だったので、俺は反論を試みることもなく大人しく頷いておきました。
lines.english: It was a reason I had no choice but to accept, so I nodded meekly without even attempting a rebuttal.

lines.japanese: 「それに休憩時間って、体よりも心の落ち着け方が大切でしょ？」
lines.english: “Besides, on a break, how you settle your mind matters more than resting your body, right?”

lines.japanese: 「そうそう。みんなで話すのが好きってやつもいれば、一人で本を読んでる時間のが休めるって奴もいんの。周りが口出すことじゃないよ」
lines.english: “Right, right. Some people like talking with everyone, and some relax better reading alone. It’s nobody else’s business.”

lines.japanese: なるほど。日和子さんの場合、読書をしている時間がいちばん心が休まるというわけですな。
lines.english: I see. For Hiyoko, then, reading was what allowed her mind to rest most fully.
